name: Statistical significance

subjectOf.text: In simple linear regressions of monthly returns on log AUM across the full sample, the AUM coefficient is statistically significant at the 5 percent level only during March through August 2012.
subjectOf.abstract: When considering the entire sample and no dummy variable, the estimated beta for the logarithm of the AUM are statistically significant at 5% level only in the period March-August 2012.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Barbara Luppi, Sandra Paterlini, Did the Dodd-Frank Act Impact Hedge Fund Performance (2014). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2389416

subjectOf.text: Adding a dummy for AUM above $150 million to the linear regressions leaves no variable significant at the 5 percent level in March 2012, and the dummy is significant only in April 2012.
subjectOf.abstract: We notice that in March 2012, no variable is statistically significant at 5% significance level while in April 2012, the dummy variable is statistically significant.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Barbara Luppi, Sandra Paterlini, Did the Dodd-Frank Act Impact Hedge Fund Performance (2014). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2389416
scope_conditions: linear model with AUM threshold dummy

subjectOf.text: The March 2012 discontinuity coefficient is the only estimate with a p-value below 5 percent; all subsequent monthly estimates are statistically insignificant.
subjectOf.abstract: Moreover, the coefficient in March 2012 is the only one with p-value smaller than 5%, while all the estimates in the following months are not significant.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Barbara Luppi, Sandra Paterlini, Did the Dodd-Frank Act Impact Hedge Fund Performance (2014). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2389416
scope_conditions: sharp RD estimates April to October 2012

subjectOf.text: The difference-in-differences interaction term identifying treated funds in 2012 is positive and statistically significant in March, April, and May 2012.
subjectOf.abstract: Table 9 also shows that the dummy variable that identifies the treatment group univocally (year 2012 and AUM>150M) is positive and statistically significant in March, April and May 2012.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Barbara Luppi, Sandra Paterlini, Did the Dodd-Frank Act Impact Hedge Fund Performance (2014). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2389416
scope_conditions: post reform dummy interacted with the AUM above $150 million dummy

subjectOf.text: All regression models show positive and predominantly statistically significant coefficients, with 18 out of 30 coefficients in the entire sample statistically significant.
subjectOf.abstract: All regression models show positive and predominantly statistically significant coefficients. 18 out of 30 coefficients in the entire sample are statistically significant.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, The Impact of Dodd-Frank Act Compliance Cost on the Hedge Fund Industry (2014). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2389423
scope_conditions: five regression specifications applied to the entire sample
